transformations.description: Copies complete accepted Alicante StopNode and StopPlace objects exactly when numeric operator stop codes already exist.
Uses the published numeric operator stop code as the stable suffix and creates one strict singleton StopPlace for every new code.
Stores 14A and 14B as separate independently ordered circular routes. Their final-to-first edges exist only through closesLoop=true; neither route is generated by reversal.
Stores Line 39 Ida and Vuelta as independent open patterns. No reverse pattern or edge is inferred.
Reconciles the historical 14A/14B street loops with operator codes available on the later/current Line 14 corridor while excluding the later Gran Vía Sur extension.
Uses exact accepted positions for reused codes; new positions use current named-stop corridor evidence, accepted neighbouring stops and AliBus nearby-stop distances where available.

warnings: The legacy map and official historical notice define the 14A/14B circular street itinerary but do not expose a complete machine-readable 2016 operator-code sequence.

The 14A/14B stop-code sequences are a documented reconciliation from the historical street itinerary, supplied diagrams, accepted identities and the later/current Line 14 corridor. They are not asserted to be a frozen 2016 stop export.
The current Line 14 Gran Vía Sur extension and its extension-only stops are intentionally excluded from this legacy circular component.
New coordinates are geographically reconciled WGS84 positions. Exact accepted objects are reused unchanged; the official GTFS archive could not be downloaded in this execution environment.
Line 39 is represented as two open directional patterns because current ordered sources expose Ida and Vuelta rather than one vehicle-cycle loop.
No genuine OpenStreetMap platform or stop_position evidence was used; StopNode.sourceReferences remains empty.
